governanceNotes: D1 batch 52 (2026-09-24): deferred. Direction and procedure-context screens recorded 2026-09-24: the located spontaneous adult literature documents the INBOUND direction rather than an outgoing consequence - a two-year series of 15 patients with paroxysmal laryngospasm (nine women and six men, mean age 56 years) found an 80% association with gastroesophageal reflux disease, with proton pump inhibitors giving complete symptom resolution in six patients and partial relief needing no further treatment in four, and with the two patients who continued to have syncopal episodes remitting after laryngeal botulinum toxin injection (PMID 17319986) - and a sleep-related laryngospasm series of 19 patients (mean age 57.2 years) in which all had at least one laryngopharyngeal reflux risk factor and 17 (89.5%) reported no further symptoms at one-year follow-up under lifestyle and proton pump therapy, the authors concluding supportive evidence for a causal relationship from laryngopharyngeal reflux to sleep-related laryngospasm (PMID 35099721). An outgoing edge authored from this identity would therefore invert the established direction of the pair.

Magnitude, target, and identity screens recorded 2026-09-24: the consequences located for spontaneous laryngospasm are syncope (two of 15 patients, case-level within the series above) and negative-pressure pulmonary edema, whose located evidence is procedural - a four-case series of post-extubation laryngospasm after general anesthesia (PMID 30591273) and a five-case series during post-anesthesia recovery in which four cases followed glossoptosis after extubation and one followed laryngeal-mask displacement (PMID 40087571), with a Chest review stating that negative-pressure pulmonary edema occurs after intense inspiratory effort against an obstructed airway, usually from upper airway infection, tumor, or laryngospasm (PMID 27063348). Those events are post-surgical-or-treatment complications rather than disease-course secondaries, the pulmonary-edema identity (draft, no authored windows) would rest on case-series-class evidence, and no catalog identity exists for syncope of this type or for aspiration. The bulk of the laryngospasm literature (anesthesia induction and extubation risk factors) describes a procedure-related event rather than a secondary condition, and the previously recorded amyotrophic-lateral-sclerosis prevalence cohort describes a different disease population. Reopening condition: a condition-specific cohort quantifying a catalog-fit secondary of spontaneous laryngospasm, creation of an airway-obstruction or pulmonary-edema pathway authored from spontaneous events, or a governance decision to author the reflux-to-laryngospasm pair on the reflux identity.
